A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, whilst the LHC will not be able to directly detect the lightest neutralinos in the focus point regions, it will be able to provide a good measurement of their properties, even in the absence of the scalar sector.

one can use the shape of the LHC dilepton invariant mass spectra to obtain good predictions of the relic density, direct search cross-section and annihilation cross-section, even without assuming which new particles are responsible for the observed kinematic features.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the LHC is capable of providing a very good prediction of astrophysical observables even when some of the relevant particles are too heavy to produce at the LHC.
the LHC is a powerful probe of dark matter properties in the absence of squarks and sleptions.

, whilst the LHC will be a very powerful probe of neutralino dark mattter in the case where the lightest neutralinos are produced in association with other new sparticles, it is also possible to make good predictions of astropysical quantities in the absence of such a production mechanism.
